summary: OpenAI announced 'Site tools', its implementation of the proposed WebMCP standard, letting websites expose functionality directly to ChatGPT agents (including Work and Codex) via the built-in desktop browser.

mechanisms.reason: The feature lets agents call a website's exposed tools directly rather than a human operating the site's UI, a form of API-based agent action replacing manual interaction.
mechanisms.quote: Site identifies/authorizes that user → Site exposes its functionality/data through WebMCP → the user’s ChatGPT Work/Codex is the LLM → ChatGPT calls your Site’s WebMCP tools with skills, assets and tools

practices.reason: Adopting WebMCP requires exposing new tool endpoints on a site and would change how ChatGPT/Codex discovers and interacts with it, but the standard is still 'proposed' and adoption is optional.
practices.quote: Site tools are ChatGPT’s implementation of the proposed WebMCP standard . With WebMCP, a website can offer useful actions directly to an AI agent alongside the interface people already use.

practices.reason: The post sketches an architecture pattern (site auth, tool exposure, agent calling) that could inform how teams design agent-website integrations, but gives no concrete implementation details or measured gains.
practices.quote: This feature is extremely versatile. For example, it could be used as an upgraded version of Custom GPTs
